title: The Hinterlands
body: The Hinterlands is a wild country of forested hills, high crags and rushing rivers northeast of Hillsbrad, running east to the cliffs above the Forbidding Sea. Long ago it lay at the heart of the Amani empire, and the ruins of forest troll cities still crown its hills. Three troll tribes remain: the Vilebranch of Jintha'Alor, who serve the blood god Hakkar, the spider-worshipping Witherbark, and the small Revantusk on the eastern coast. Into this troll country came the Wildhammer dwarves, who built Aerie Peak and bonded with the gryphons of the crags.

title: Aerie Peak
body: Aerie Peak is the home of the Wildhammer clan, raised on a crag after the clan found Grim Batol tainted and refused King Bronzebeard's offer of a home. Unlike their cousins, the Wildhammers built above ground, and at the crest of the town stands the great gryphon aviary. High Thane Falstad Wildhammer rules here, and his people give outsiders a blunt welcome: they are no part of the Alliance, they say, and judge strangers by deeds alone.

parts.body: Since the draenei joined the Alliance, an envoy from the Exodar waits here for an audience with the High Thane, and has found that calling the Wildhammers wary of outsiders is quite an understatement.

title: Quel'Danil Lodge
body: Quel'Danil Lodge is a high elven outpost in the woods east of Aerie Peak, held by the Highvale elves, who keep their own watch on the Witherbark trolls and share what they learn with other races. The Highvale have made friends of the Wildhammers, and the Revantusk trolls hate them for it. Scouts, marksmen and rangers guard the grounds, and a captured Witherbark troll sits caged within.

title: Shadra'Alor
body: Shadra'Alor is the temple city of the Witherbark trolls, a cluster of old temples in the southern Hinterlands where the tribe keeps the worship of its spider god. Broodguard spiders nest among the ruins beside Witherbark sadists and callers. Not every troll here is Witherbark: an Atal'ai priest, cast out of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows, now lives among them in exile.

parts.body: The city's name holds the god's own. Her true name is Elortha no Shadra, to be spoken only in whispers, and from her the Witherbark draw their most potent venom; read at the altar here, a spell written in that name will call Shadra herself into the world.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Shadra'Alor (main Witherbark settlement, Shadra summoned there)

parts.body: Upon one of its altars lie the bones of Featherbeard, the revered gryphon trainer of Aerie Peak, who came alone in search of eggs stolen from the aeries, a map of the city still clutched in his hand.

title: Jintha'Alor
body: Jintha'Alor, named for an ancient Amani leader, is the second largest forest troll city after Zul'Aman and the capital of the Vilebranch. From its summit Vile Priestess Hexx serves Hakkar the blood god, and vessels of tainted blood scattered through the city fill the tribe with his ferocity and madness. Captives are kept here for sacrifice, and in a cave behind the amphitheater rests an ancient egg, a relic of the days when trolls ruled vast empires.

parts.body: The Vilebranch prey on the weaker Revantusk. In a midnight raid they carried off Elder Torntusk, the Revantusk chieftain, and Hexx is said to be preparing him as a sacrifice to the blood god.

title: Seradane
body: In the northeast of the Hinterlands rises Seradane, one of the four great trees whose portals open into the Emerald Dream. The green dragonflight has made the surrounding forest its home: its dragonspawn patrol the glades in bands, and the drakes Rothos and Dreamtracker keep watch nearby, suffering no intruder to come near the portal.

parts.body: Something darker has come through the portal as well. Lethon, once among Ysera's most trusted lieutenants and now twisted by nightmare, lurks beneath the boughs, his scales darkened and his power turned to shadow.

title: Revantusk Village
body: On the southeastern coast lies Revantusk Village, home of the smallest and weakest of the region's three troll tribes. Scorned by the other forest trolls for their loyalty to the Horde, the Revantusk never formally rejoined it under Thrall but keep a pact of friendship with it, and wind riders link the village to Horde lands. Elder Torntusk is their chieftain and Primal Torntusk his mate, and they have long feuded with the Wildhammers of Aerie Peak.

parts.body: Elder Torntusk came home from Jintha'Alor, freed from his shackles atop the city, and sent word ahead to his mate that he was returning to her.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Revantusk_tribe (southeast coast; attacked by other forest trolls for loyalty to the Horde; declined to rejoin, pact of friendship)

parts.body: Primal Torntusk lifted the dark energy of the blood god from the Vilebranch, but only for now: even if the Vile Priestess falls, she warns, another will soon take her place.

title: Falstad Wildhammer
body: Falstad Wildhammer is High Thane of the Wildhammer clan. After the Second War he led a small flight of gryphon riders patrolling the shores of Lordaeron, and it was Falstad and his riders who carried the mage Rhonin and his companions across the sea to Khaz Modan. He fought in the final battle at Grim Batol that freed the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza, and when Kurdran Wildhammer left for Draenor, Falstad stayed behind at Aerie Peak and succeeded him.
